items.summary: Abstract Background: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and stable coronary artery disease (SCAD) present overlapping clinical phenotypes, yet mandate divergent therapeutic strategies—urgent revascularization versus pharmacological optimization. Current diagnostic reliance on high-sensitivity cardiac troponin dynamic monitoring introduces hazardous delays (4–6 hours detection window) and yields false negatives in 20% of…
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and stable coronary artery disease (SCAD) present overlapping clinical phenotypes, yet mandate divergent therapeutic strategies—urgent revascularization versus pharmacological optimization. Current diagnostic reliance on high-sensitivity cardiac troponin dynamic monitoring introduces hazardous delays (4–6 hours detection window) and yields false negatives in 20% of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation index (FAI), quantifying vascular inflammation through computed tomography (CT) attenuation changes in pericoronary fat, offers mechanistic insight into coronary plaque destabilization. However, the translational pathway from this biomarker to clinically actionable decision support remains incompletely realized, particularly regarding integration with established anatomical and functional parameters and explicit clinical interpretability. Hypothesis: A mechanistically grounded, multi-dimensional nomogram combining FAI with coronary CT angiography (CCTA)-derived anatomical stenosis (%DS), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and smoking status—rendered interpretable through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)—would achieve robust ACS-SCAD discrimination while providing transparent, auditable decision logic suitable for clinical implementation. Methods: In this prospective diagnostic accuracy study adhering to TRIPOD 2019 guidelines, 388 patients (ACS 117 [30.2%], SCAD 271 [69.8%]) underwent CCTA with standardized FAI, %DS, and LVEF acquisition. Stratified randomization (7:3) produced training (n=271) and validation (n=117) sets with preserved outcome distribution. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with 10-fold stratified cross-validation compared lambda.min versus lambda.1se selection criteria, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, Brier score, and decision curve analysis. KernelSHAP parsed individualized decision contributions. Regulatory-readiness was evaluated through predetermined change control documentation and explanation stability assessment. Results: LASSO lambda.min retained %DS, FAI, LVEF, RVEF, and smoking; lambda.1se selected only %DS and FAI. Final model incorporated %DS, FAI, LVEF, and smoking based on mechanistic non-overlap (RVEF-LVEF functional redundancy) and epidemiological importance. Multivariable analysis demonstrated %DS (OR 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01–1.04, P < 0.001) and FAI (OR 1.04, 95% CI: 1.02–1.06, P < 0.001) as positive ACS predictors; LVEF as protective (OR 0.96, 95% CI: 0.92–0.99, P = 0.032); smoking as marginally non-significant (OR 1.83, 95% CI: 0.87–3.86, P = 0.110) but incrementally contributory. Nomogram achieved AUC 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82–0.91) in training and 0.82 (95% CI: 0.75–0.90) in validation. Optimal cutoff 0.291 (Youden index) yielded training sensitivity 0.80, specificity 0.82, negative predictive value 0.91; validation sensitivity 0.73, specificity 0.72, negative predictive value 0.83. Calibration was satisfactory (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.347 and P = 0.405). Decision curve analysis demonstrated net benefit across threshold probability 0.10–0.55. SHAP analysis established a mechanistic hierarchy: %DS and FAI as dominant drivers (mean |SHAP| 0.75 and 0.70), LVEF as a functional protective modifier (0.35), and smoking as a behavioral risk stratifier (0.20). Individual force plots enabled case-level explanation with documented contribution stability. Conclusions: The %DS-FAI-LVEF-smoking nomogram achieves favorable ACS discriminatory accuracy with acceptable generalization. SHAP-enhanced interpretability satisfies emerging transparency requirements for artificial intelligence-enabled medical devices, supporting regulatory-ready clinical translation. Translational Significance: This study bridges the critical T1–T2 translational gap by converting perivascular inflammation biology (FAI) into an evidence-based diagnostic tool validated for a specific clinical decision context. The "one-stop" CCTA acquisition strategy—yielding anatomical, inflammatory, and functional data from a single examination—addresses implementation barriers in time-critical emergency settings. Explicit SHAP-based explainability exceeds current "black box" machine learning limitations, aligning with FDA and EMA guidance on predetermined change control and transparency documentation for clinical artificial intelligence. These design elements collectively reduce translational friction from research prototype to prospective clinical trials and eventual regulatory approval, advancing precision coronary care through mechanism-informed, transparently interpretable decision support.

items.abstract: Background: The microbiota–gut–brain axis provides an emerging framework for understanding neuropsychiatric disorders. Depression and addiction, despite substantial comorbidity, are frequently investigated separately. This review examines whether gut dysbiosis contributes to vulnerability, symptom persistence and recovery through shared inflammatory, endocrine, metabolic and reward-related mechanisms. Methods A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and PsycINFO, supplemented by citation searching. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta-analyses, human cohorts, randomised trials and mechanistic studies. Evidence was evaluated for methodological quality, confounding, replication, biological plausibility and clinical relevance. Results Convergent evidence implicates altered short-chain fatty acid production, intestinal barrier dysfunction, dysregulated tryptophan–kynurenine metabolism, systemic inflammation, hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal-axis disturbance and altered affective and reward signalling. Human evidence is strongest for major depressive disorder and alcohol use disorder, whereas evidence involving opioids, psychostimulants, cannabis and polysubstance use remains comparatively limited. Dietary interventions, probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics and faecal microbiota transplantation demonstrate preliminary therapeutic potential. However, methodological heterogeneity, uncertain causality, limited replication and insufficient evidence of sustained benefit prevent routine clinical recommendation. Digital phenotyping, wearable technologies and artificial intelligence may facilitate integration of microbial, metabolic, behavioural and longitudinal clinical information, although prospective validation and demonstrated clinical utility remain limited. Conclusions The proposed Microbiota–Gut–Brain–Reward framework conceptualises dysbiosis as a potentially modifiable contributor rather than an independent cause of depression or addiction. Clinical translation requires longitudinal multi-omic research, harmonised methodologies, mechanistically informed trials and integration with established pharmacological, psychological and social interventions. Digitally enabled precision approaches may support personalised recovery monitoring, provided interpretability, privacy, equity and clinical governance are prioritised. The United Arab Emirates offers opportunities for culturally responsive translational research, although implementation must remain evidence-driven, ethically governed and subject to rigorous prospective evaluation before clinical adoption.

items.abstract: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by chronic cerebral hypoperfusion and cognitive decline, yet the role of fatty acid metabolism in its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Integrated transcriptomic profiling was combined with network-based analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning to uncover key fatty acid metabolism-associated molecular features associated with VaD. Single-cell RNA sequencing, intercellular communication inference, and in silico perturbation analyses were applied to define immune-stromal interactions. Potential therapeutic compounds were evaluated using molecular docking and dynamics simulations. We identified three VaD-related fatty acid metabolism genes (VaD-FAMRGs), namely PNPLA3, HSP90AA1, and ALB, which showed consistent diagnostic performance across multiple computational approaches and were associated with lipid metabolism, inflammatory processes, and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Functional enrichment, single-cell RNA sequencing, and in silico gene perturbation analyses provided exploratory insights into the potential associations of these candidate genes with lipid transport, metabolic regulation, synaptic maintenance, and immune-inflammatory processes. Cell-cell communication analysis further revealed activation of the ANGPTL signaling axis, suggesting impaired endothelial-glial interactions driven by lipid metabolic dysregulation. Regulatory network analysis identified key transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulators, including REST, miR-155-5p, and miR-21-5p, which may coordinately modulate VaD-FAMRG expression. Drug repurposing analysis highlighted quercetin as a candidate compound with predicted interactions with all three hub proteins, supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. These findings suggest that dysregulated fatty acid metabolism may be associated with the development and progression of VaD through coordinated metabolic, inflammatory, and neurovascular mechanisms. This study provides a systems-level framework for understanding the underlying pathological processes and establishes a theoretical basis for future mechanistic and experimental validation.

items.abstract: Recent advances in precision oncology fueled the development of nanotherapeutics,​ molecularly targeted drugs, engineered immunotherapies, RNA therapeutics, and smart biomaterials for more selective cancer treatment. However, long-term therapeutic responses remain restricted by interconnected adaptive mechanisms, including ABC transporter-mediated drug efflux, dysregulated signaling pathways, apoptosis evasion, immune escape, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and tumor microenvironment​ remodeling. In this review article, these processes are collectively framed as tumor-mediated molecular hijacking, describing malignant cell exploitation and microenvironmental pathways that promote multidrug resistance and therapeutic failure. The review critically examines nanotherapeutic and advanced biotherapeutic strategies to counteract these mechanisms, including functionalized nanocarriers, antibody-drug conjugates, CAR-T cells, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy, immune checkpoint blockade, mesenchymal stem-cell (MSC)-based therapeutics, CRISPR-mediated genome editing, bispecific T-cell engagers, and RNA-based approaches. Particular focus includes drug-delivery elements such as tumour penetration, intracellular trafficking, controlled release, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, and critical formulation attributes, as well as translational challenges such as manufacturability, scalability, reproducibility, stability, safety, and regulatory feasibility. Emerging biofabrication approaches enable the fabrication of adaptive and personalized delivery systems, while artificial intelligence and machine learning are utilized as tools for structure-guided design, nanocarrier optimization, treatment-response prediction, and patient-specific digital-twin modelling. This paper combines tumor-mediated molecular hijacking with drug delivery technology at the forefront and translational aspects to create a comprehensive platform for clinically relevant precision cancer therapeutics.Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

items.abstract: Machine learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) is an emerging paradigm of protein design where ML models trained on experimental data are used to guide exploration of a protein fitness landscape. Building an MLDE pipeline involves many design choices across the design-build-test-learn loop ranging from data collection strategies to modeling. The cost of collecting experimental data makes benchmarking every component of these pipelines prohibitively difficult, necessitating the development of synthetic landscapes. In this work, we develop a framework called SLIP ("Synthetic Landscape Inference for Proteins") for constructing synthetic landscapes with tunable difficulty based on Potts models. This framework can be extended to any protein family for which there is a sequence alignment. We show that our tuning framework provides landscapes sufficiently challenging to benchmark MLDE pipelines. SLIP is open-source and is available at https://github.com/google-research/slip.

items.abstract: The human gastrointestinal (GI) microbiota is a complex and dynamic microbial ecosystem that plays a fundamental role in maintaining host metabolism, immune homeostasis, intestinal barrier integrity, and protection against pathogenic microorganisms. Disruption of this microbial community, known as gut dysbiosis, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous GI and systemic diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), Clostridioides difficile infection, obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, colorectal cancer, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease. Although antibiotics remain indispensable for the treatment of bacterial infections, their indiscriminate use frequently disrupts gut microbial composition, reduces microbial diversity, promotes opportunistic pathogen overgrowth, and accelerates the emergence of antimicrobial resistance. These limitations have stimulated increasing interest in microbiota-targeted interventions as safer and more sustainable therapeutic strategies. Probiotics and prebiotics have emerged as promising approaches for restoring gut microbial homeostasis through complementary mechanisms. Probiotics inhibit pathogen colonization, enhance intestinal barrier function, produce antimicrobial metabolites, and modulate host immune responses. Prebiotics selectively stimulate the growth and metabolic activity of beneficial microorganisms, promoting the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) that support intestinal and systemic health. Increasing evidence from experimental studies, randomized clinical trials, and meta-analyses demonstrates that these microbiota-directed interventions can reduce antibiotic-associated diarrhea, improve symptoms of IBD and IBS, enhance Helicobacter pylori eradication, decrease recurrence of C. difficile infection, and contribute to the management of several metabolic disorders. Despite these promising findings, important challenges remain regarding strain specificity, optimal dosage, treatment duration, product standardization, regulatory oversight, and interindividual variability in treatment response. Emerging advances in metagenomics, metabolomics, artificial intelligence, and precision medicine are facilitating the development of personalized microbiome-based therapies that may further enhance clinical outcomes. This review critically summarizes the current understanding of GI microbiota dysbiosis, discusses the mechanisms through which probiotics and prebiotics restore microbial balance, evaluates their clinical applications as alternatives or adjuncts to antibiotic therapy, and highlights existing challenges and future research directions for microbiome-based therapeutics.

items.abstract: Objectives Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, accompanied by increased iron accumulation, particularly in the nigrosome-1 subregion. Differentiating neurodegenerative disorders like PD from non-neurodegenerative causes of parkinsonism can be challenging. In clinically uncertain parkinsonian syndrome (CUPS), dopamine transporter (DAT)-single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) can aid diagnosis. However, susceptibility map-weighted imaging (SMWI) provides a promising magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alternative. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy and reliability of visual SMWI assessment by radiologists in CUPS and the added value of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic software. Materials and methods Patients with CUPS who underwent DAT-SPECT between January 2019 and July 2023 were included. Four radiologists, blinded to clinical symptoms and diagnosis, visually rated nigrosome-1 on axial SMWI reconstructions as normal, unclear, or abnormal. After the initial assessment, the radiologists re-evaluated the scans with AI-driven software assistance, designed to classify and quantify nigrosome-1 integrity. The reference standard was the final clinical diagnosis incorporating DAT-SPECT results. Results One hundred eighty patients were included (mean age 67.9, range 31-86, 120 males), 84 with neurodegenerative and 96 with non-neurodegenerative parkinsonism. Mean diagnostic accuracy was 80% (range 73-83%), with substantial inter-rater reliability (Fleiss κ 0.65). With software assistance, diagnostic accuracy improved to 87% (range 85-91%), and inter-rater agreement increased to almost perfect (Fleiss κ 0.86). Conclusion SMWI, particularly with AI-driven software assistance, is a promising and accessible MRI-based technique that may support the diagnostic workup in clinically uncertain parkinsonism, aiding the distinction between neurodegenerative and non-neurodegenerative causes. Key points Question Can susceptibility map-weighted imaging (SMWI) reliably differentiate neurodegenerative from non-neurodegenerative parkinsonism in clinically uncertain cases, and does artificial intelligence (AI)-driven software assistance improve radiologist performance? Findings Visual assessment had an accuracy of 80%, with substantial inter-rater reliability. AI-driven software assistance increased accuracy to 87% and improved inter-rater reliability. Relevance statement SMWI can differentiate neurodegenerative from non-neurodegenerative parkinsonism in clinically uncertain cases and may support the diagnostic process by offering an accessible MRI-based technique, facilitating an efficient diagnostic workup, and enabling early diagnosis in clinically uncertain parkinsonism.

items.abstract: Background General practitioners face high complexity in clinical decision-making. Large language models (LLMs) may support clinical reasoning, but their impact on decision-making processes and postgraduate medical training remains unclear. This qualitative study aims to explore General Practice (GP) trainee's use of LLMs in clinical reasoning and their educational needs. Materials and methods GP trainees were recruited and interviewed with semi-structured interview-guide. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed qualitatively. Results Seventeen GP trainees participated (mean interview duration: 38 min; range: 21-63 min). AI was perceived as a tool to augment and accelerate clinical decision-making, while potential risks of deskilling were identified. Participants reported a lack of structured AI education and expressed a need for its integration into postgraduate training. Discussion Participants perceived AI primarily as a supportive tool that can complement clinical reasoning and improve access to medical knowledge. At the same time, they identified potential risks, including overreliance on AI-generated information and possible effects on the development of clinical expertise. These findings suggest that postgraduate medical training should address AI-related competencies, including critical appraisal, ethical responsibility and appropriate integration of AI into clinical decision-making. Conclusion AI is already part of clinical practice among GP trainees, offering opportunities to support learning and clinical reasoning while raising concerns about overreliance and critical appraisal. Postgraduate medical training in GP should therefore incorporate structured AI competencies to ensure responsible, reflective and patient-centered use of AI.

items.abstract: Clinical large language model (LLM) deployment is shifting from feasibility to liability, while current guidance largely treats model behavior as a control problem. We tested whether decision-style system prompts shift clinical action thresholds when clinical facts are held constant, and whether these shifts are consistent across settings and models. We defined nine physician personas by crossing three ethical orientations (duty-based, care-based, utilitarian) with three cognitive styles (intuitive, integrative, analytic). Twenty open-weight LLMs were evaluated on 2500 simulated emergency department vignettes and 2500 MIMIC-IV-Note discharge summaries. For each text, models answered five binary decision items (safety, autonomy, treatment, resource use, follow-up). Each condition was repeated ten times, yielding 5,000,000 total decisions. Under baseline prompting, models answered "Yes" to 42.8% of decisions. Persona prompts shifted affirmative rates from 36.9% to 46.4%, a 9.5 percentage-point swing under fixed clinical evidence. Effects were largest in autonomy and treatment and were consistent across corpora (85.7% directional agreement; r = 0.82 for effect sizes). Susceptibility varied by model (4.9-16.1 points), with no consistent protection from medical fine-tuning or model size. Decision-style system prompts reliably change clinical action thresholds in LLMs under fixed evidence. Prompting is a policy-setting layer, not just a communication layer, and should be treated as a first-class deployment configuration.

items.abstract: Background Late-onset sepsis (LOS) causes morbidity and mortality in very-low birthweight (VLBW) neonates. We previously developed a machine learning model, the Pulse Oximetry Warning System (POWS), to predict LOS in the next 24 h. The neonatal Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (nSOFA) score predicts sepsis mortality. We hypothesized that POWS scores would differentiate severe LOS events, defined by nSOFA >4, from milder events. Methods We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study including VLBW infants diagnosed with culture-confirmed LOS with continuous vital sign data available. Mixed-effects regression was used to examine the association between POWS and nSOFA. Results We analyzed 89 LOS episodes in 84 VLBW infants. Severe sepsis (nSOFA >4 within 48 h of blood culture) occurred in 27 (30%) episodes. Mean POWS scores were higher in the 24 h before severe LOS than non-severe LOS. POWS rose more steeply in the hours before sepsis diagnosis among infants with severe LOS. Conclusion POWS scores, predicting risk of LOS in the next 24 h, have a significantly higher rate of rise in severe episodes as compared to less severe episodes as measured by nSOFA. This result adds to evidence that POWS could prompt earlier intervention that improves sepsis outcomes. Impact Late-onset sepsis (LOS) is a leading cause of death and disability in premature infants. The Pulse Oximetry Warning System (POWS) uses continuous heart rate and oxygen saturation data to predict sepsis up to 24 h before clinical diagnosis. This study demonstrates that POWS rises more steeply before severe sepsis episodes, as defined by the neonatal Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (nSOFA) score, than before milder episodes. POWS thus may provide earlier warning of the most severe sepsis events, potentially enabling earlier intervention in this vulnerable population.

items.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) are widely used for noninvasive brain monitoring in clinical and cognitive applications, where machine learning-based classification has become increasingly prevalent. Alongside algorithmic advances, a growing body of literature reports signal-derived metrics as digital biomarkers; however, their interpretation, validity, and comparability remain strongly dependent on target definition, processing pipelines, and evaluation practices. This review provides a structured overview of EEG- and fNIRS-based classification studies, with a particular focus on signal processing workflows and biomarker extraction. The reviewed literature is organized around key stages of the analytical pipeline, including target formulation, data preprocessing, feature extraction, and validation. Common feature families-spanning spectral, temporal, connectivity-based, network-level, and hemodynamic representations-are summarized and discussed in relation to their typical applications and limitations. The main contribution is an evidence-based distinction between signal features and credible candidate biomarkers. Reliability, analytical robustness, external generalization, and interpretability are considered within the intended context of use. Clinical utility is assessed separately from predictive performance. Across 117 primary studies, most measures remained candidate biomarkers; only four studies were assigned to independent clinical validation, with qualifications, and none evaluated clinical utility.

items.abstract: Classifying viral pathogens from next-generation sequencing (NGS) data is central to diagnosis and genomic surveillance. Most deep learning classifiers, however, read only a fixed window at the start of each genome, typically a few hundred to a few thousand base pairs, and so ignore more than 95% of the sequence of large DNA viruses such as monkeypox virus (MPV) and herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1). We refer to this problem as Truncation Blindness. Here we present Viro-BERT, which splits a complete genome into overlapping 512-token windows, encodes each window with a shared DistilBERT encoder, and averages the window-level class probabilities in a Late Fusion Consensus layer. Because the windows are processed independently, memory use does not grow with genome length. We compared Viro-BERT with one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) and RoBERTa baselines on 14 viral classes, using the same segmentation and training protocol for all models. Viro-BERT reached 96.79% accuracy and a macro-F1 score of 96.17%. We then added random substitution noise to the test genomes. At 5% noise, the accuracy of the 1D-CNN fell by 5.57 percentage points, whereas Viro-BERT still classified 93.68% of genomes correctly. Positional and attention analyses on HSV-1 showed that Viro-BERT uses diagnostic signal from across the genome rather than from its 5' end alone. These results indicate that whole-genome context is needed for viral classifiers that remain reliable on noisy clinical data.

items.abstract: Background and objective Rapid growth in medical literature limits traditional systematic review methods, particularly in high-volume fields like maternity care. This paper presents a novel methodological approach using a hybrid workflow that combines Large Language Model (LLM) semantic data extraction with programmatic filtering to automate title and abstract screening. Methods The workflow was deployed on a high-volume clinical dataset (51,281 records retrieved from six databases) as a validation case study. Google Gemini 1.5-pro and 2.5-flash extracted 12 structured semantic variables, followed by a seven-stage rule-based filtering pipeline to determine eligibility. The workflow's accuracy was validated against a large-scale manual audit. Results The workflow reduced the human manual screening burden by 96%. Validation demonstrated an estimated sensitivity of 89.9% (95% confidence interval; CI 87.3-92.1%), specificity of 96.4% (95% CI 96.2-96.5%), and false negative rate of 0.18% (95% CI 0.09-0.35%), achieving accuracy comparable to dual-human review. Total API expenditure was US$458.73. Subgroup analysis found no change in screening accuracy after changing LLM. Discussion This approach offers a scalable, transparent, cost-effective, and model-agnostic solution for evidence synthesis. By decoupling data extraction from inclusion logic, researchers maintain granular control over eligibility criteria, supporting scalable evidence synthesis and living systematic reviews.

items.abstract: Background Machine learning (ML) methods may improve prediction of individual risk of mortality risk after congenital heart surgery (CHD) by identifying nonlinear relationships/novel combinations of variables. Improved risk discrimination may improve outcomes by optimizing resource allocation and patient surveillance. Methods Children and adolescents (age≤18 years) undergoing CHD surgery at Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium hospitals 9/1/2014-12/30/2019 were studied. Non-collinear potential predictors were identified empirically and used to create a logistic regression risk (LR) model (mimicking traditional risk-adjustment models) and ML (random forest and gradient boosting model) models. Model performance was evaluated using net reclassification index (NRI), the proportion of subjects in which either the absolute risk category or estimated risk relative to other subjects changed between each model and one composed only of STAT category as the primary outcome. This metric reflects how often a model changes how a clinician views the risk of a patient relative to a parsimonious model and provides some measure of the utility of these models. Secondary analyses compared overall model fit. Results In total 51,475 operative encounters from 52 hospitals were studied. Subjects were 45% female, 20% neonates, and 5% underwent STAT 5 operations. C-statistics and Brier scores did not differ significantly between ML and LR models. For absolute risk categorires, point estimates for NRI between ML-models and STAT category (0.76 95%CI: 0.68-0.83) suggested at best modest improvements compared to logistic regression model (0.75 95%CI 0.67-0.83), but the difference was not significant. Similarly, for rankings of risk within the cohort, NRI for ML models (0.26 95%CI: 0.19-0.32) was not significantly different to that for the LR model (0.24 95%CI: 0.17-0.33). Conclusion ML derived models did not improve overall model fit. Magnitude of improvement in reclassification was at best modest and not statistically significant. Future research is necessary to evaluate the added values of incorporating more comprehensive data and/or advanced computational techniques and use of reclassification in risk prediction.

items.abstract: Background Existing prediction models for stroke-heart syndrome (SHS) after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) have limited generalizability due to population heterogeneity. Objective To develop and validate a generalizable risk prediction model for SHS following AIS. Methods A retrospective cohort of 1404 AIS patients from the MIMIC-IV database was utilized. After feature selection, 14 machine learning algorithms were evaluated. All algorithms were trained under identical preprocessing with per-algorithm automatically tuned hyperparameters and evaluated by five-fold cross-validation and hold-out internal validation. The final model-a logistic regression-based nomogram-was externally validated on an independent single-center cohort (n = 321). Performance was assessed by discrimination (area under the curve [AUC]), calibration (calibration curves, Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis). Model interpretability was augmented using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results Seven early-admission predictors were identified: age, heart rate, prothrombin time, blood urea nitrogen, Glasgow Coma Scale score, respiratory rate, and body temperature. The model demonstrated strong, consistent discrimination across datasets: training AUC=0.789, internal validation AUC=0.802, and external validation AUC=0.810. Calibration was good on internal validation (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.614) but showed external under-dispersion (slope 1.72, P = 0.004); local recalibration is indicated. Decision curve analysis confirmed clinical net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. Conclusion We developed and validated a parsimonious SHS risk prediction model using seven early-admission indicators that overcomes the generalizability limitations of prior tools through multi-algorithm validation and external testing. Relying on routine clinical variables, this tool facilitates rapid risk stratification for precision prevention, though future prospective validation in diverse populations is warranted.

items.abstract: Fatty acid composition is a major determinant of nutritional quality, oxidative stability and functional value of oilseed crops. It is shaped by coordinated plastidial fatty acid synthesis, endoplasmic reticulum-associated desaturation and elongation, acyl editing, triacylglycerol assembly and lipid turnover in seed. This review summarizes the metabolic basis of fatty acid diversity of edible oil in major and specialty oilseed crops, then examines how genetic architecture and omics-assisted discovery have accelerated the identification of loci, alleles and candidate genes controlling fatty acid composition. We emphasize a design framework that links locus discovery to allele prioritization, targeted editing, pathway engineering and field deployment. Linkage mapping, bulked segregant sequencing, genome wide association studies, transcriptomics, proteomics and pangenome analyses are increasingly revealing both canonical genes and previously unrecognized structural or regulatory variation. We further discuss improvement strategies ranging from conventional and marker-assisted breeding to single-gene editing, transgenic manipulation and multigene synthetic biology. Finally, we highlight emerging opportunities in population genomics, underutilized oil crop mining, artificial intelligence (AI)-guided enzyme and promoter design, and agronomic evaluation. Collectively, these advances are shifting oilseed improvement from empirical selection toward rational, pathway-informed design of fatty acid profiles, while emphasizing the continuing need for biochemical validation and field-level performance assessment.

items.abstract: Background Allergic rhinitis (AR) is characterized by a T helper 2 (Th2)-cell-mediated immune imbalance, yet its upstream molecular drivers remain poorly defined. Interleukin-17 receptor B (IL-17Rb) has been implicated in type 2 inflammation, but its precise functional role and mechanism in AR pathogenesis are unclear. Objective This study aimed to identify key immunoregulatory genes in AR via bioinformatics and to comprehensively elucidate the functional role and mechanisms of IL-17Rb using both in vivo animal and in vitro cellular models. Methods Candidate genes were screened using GEO datasets and machine learning. An HDM-induced AR murine model and in vitro cell models were utilized. AAV-mediated IL-17Rb knockdown or overexpression, alongside a specific STAT6 inhibitor (AS1517499), were employed. Evaluations included nasal symptoms, histopathology, STAT6 activation, and parameters of Th2 inflammation alongside the Th1/Th17/Treg balance (IL-4/5/13, IFN-γ, IL-17A, IL-10). Results Bioinformatics identified IL-17Rb as a pivotal upregulated gene in AR, correlating with Th2 infiltration (r = 0.74). In vivo, IL-17Rb knockdown alleviated AR symptoms, eosinophil/mast cell infiltration, and type 2 cytokine release. Importantly, it rectified the AR-associated immune imbalance by restoring IFN-γ (Th1) and IL-10 (Treg) while reducing IL-17A (Th17). Conversely, IL-17Rb overexpression exacerbated Th2 inflammation and STAT6 phosphorylation. Co-administration of AS1517499 successfully abrogated these overexpression-induced effects, confirming a STAT6-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, in vitro blockade of IL-17Rb inhibited IL-25-promoted Th2 differentiation and STAT6 activation. Conclusion IL-17Rb is a critical upstream immunoregulator in AR, driving STAT6-dependent Th2 inflammation and broadly modulating the Th1/Th17/Treg balance. Targeting the IL-17Rb/STAT6 axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy.

items.abstract: Purpose Cardiometabolic disease and obesity are important factors when considering breast cancer risk and survivorship. We aimed to utilize a fully automated deep learning algorithm to evaluate CT-derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in patients with breast cancer. Methods We applied fully automated deep learning algorithms to derive cardiometabolic markers from baseline computed tomography (CT) abdomen scans of females with breast cancer diagnosed between 2016 - 2018 at Johns Hopkins. Results Among 127 females (64.6% postmenopausal; 57.5% White and 26.8% Black race), BMI (body mass index) was positively correlated with CT-derived adipose tissue area and​ muscle area, and negatively correlated with liver intensity, but not associated with presence of aortic calcification. However, myosteatosis and menopausal status outperformed BMI as clinical markers of cardiometabolic health​ in breast cancer, as they were associated with both adiposity (especially visceral adiposity) and the presence of aortic calcification, with myosteatosis also being associated with liver steatosis. Conclusion Artificial intelligence algorithms can feasibly and directly quantify body composition, liver fat, and abdominal aortic plaque, and be a tool in evaluating metabolic disease risk in patients with breast cancer.

items.abstract: Purpose To assess the feasibility of personalized tumor-masked structural connectomics combined with interpretable machine learning (ML) for differentiating low-grade gliomas (LGG) from high-grade gliomas (HGG), and to identify candidate tract-specific connectomic biomarkers of glioma aggressiveness. Methods Thirty-five patients with histopathologically confirmed gliomas (20 LGG, 15 HGG) underwent preoperative diffusion tensor imaging and T1-weighted MRI. Tumor-masked probabilistic tractography was used to reconstruct individualized structural connectomes based on 50 white matter (WM) tract labels. We evaluated 296 graph-theoretical features using sequential feature selection and Random Forest classification within a strictly isolated nested cross-validation framework. We used SHAP analysis for model interpretation. Sensitivity analyses compared clinical-radiological, connectomic, and combined feature sets. Results The leak-free pure connectomics model achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.814 ± 0.327 (95% CI, 0.500-1.000), with a macro-F1 score of 0.786 ± 0.265. Restricting the analysis to non-zero connectomic features yielded a mean AUC of 0.833 ± 0.167. The clinical-radiological model achieved a mean AUC of 0.817 ± 0.149, while the combined clinical-radiological and connectomic model showed the highest point estimate (AUC, 0.933 ± 0.109; 95% CI, 0.798-1.068). SHAP analysis highlighted the sagittal stratum, medial lemniscus, and superior fronto-occipital fasciculus among the most informative WM pathways. Conclusion Tumor-masked structural connectomics combined with interpretable ML demonstrated preliminary feasibility for identifying candidate imaging biomarkers associated with glioma aggressiveness in neuroradiological practice. These findings are exploratory and represent internal estimates from a single cohort; external validation in independent, multi-center cohorts is required before any potential clinical application.

items.abstract: Objectives To develop radiomics model, 2D deep learning (2D DL) model, 2.5D deep learning (2.5D DL) model, 3D deep learning (3D DL) model, and their fusion models to differentiate spinal tuberculosis (STB) from spinal metastasis (SM) based on MR imaging. Methods This retrospective study included 186 STB patients and 219 SM patients. Patients from three hospitals were divided into a training set (n = 191), an internal test set (n = 82) and an external test set (n = 132). Using the ResNet50 network pre-trained leveraging the ImageNet dataset, we developed 2D, 2.5D, and 3D deep learning models based on MR imaging. We constructed the radiomics model by using PyRadiomics to extract radiomics features. Deep learning models and radiomics model were used to construct two fusion models: the feature-based model (Rad_DL_FB) and the decision-based model (Rad_DL_DB). And the accuracy of these models was validated. Results In the internal test set, the Rad_DL_FB model demonstrated superior performance compared to other models, achieving the highest AUC of 0.971 (95% CI: 0.953-0.989) and accuracy of 0.927. In the external test set, the Rad_DL_DB model demonstrated superior performance compared to other models, achieving the highest AUC of 0.961 (95% CI: 0.940-0.982) and accuracy of 0.909. Furthermore, fusion-model assistance significantly improved the diagnostic accuracy of junior spine surgeons and narrowed the observed performance gap between junior and senior surgeons. Conclusion The fusion models including Rad_DL_FB model and Rad_DL_DB model, which integrates radiomics features and deep learning features of different dimensions, can effectively differentiate STB from SM, thereby assisting clinicians in making clinical decisions.

items.abstract: Looped Transformers improve parameter efficiency by repeatedly applying the same Transformer layers. During autoregressive decoding, however, generating each token requires several sequential passes through these layers, leading to high decoding latency. Pipelined self-speculative methods use shallow-loop predictions to process tokens at different loops in the same batch, but each token must reach the drafting depth before the next can enter the pipeline. We introduce LoopFill, a training-free speculative decoding algorithm for looped LLM that combines multi-token suffix drafts with shallow-loop predictions in a single draft tree. Both drafters contribute to one tree, so a suffix lookup can immediately extend a shallow prediction and several future tokens can enter the pipeline together. The shared block computes the highest-scoring draft candidates at different loop depths in one batch, and full-depth verification preserves the model's autoregressive output distribution. Across seven benchmarks, LoopFill's average speedup over greedy autoregressive decoding is 5.85times on Ouro-2.6B and 5.13times on Huginn-3.5B. The speedups exceed those of LoopAhead, the strongest baseline, by \(40\%\) on Ouro-2.6B and \(25\%\) on Huginn-3.5B.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become central to neuro-oncological imaging, impacting clinical and scientific workflows. In clinical practice, AI-based image reconstruction and noise reduction expedite the generation of advanced multiparametric MRI and PET scans. Automated segmentation and volumetric analysis improve reproducibility, speed, and standardization of tumor quantification and response assessment. In research, large language and multimodal models extract structured information from radiology reports and medical records. Collaborative initiatives, such as BraTS and FeTS, have established standardized, privacy-compliant frameworks for large-scale quantitative analyses. Tumor-specific applications include noninvasive molecular profiling in gliomas, grading and recurrence prediction in meningiomas, detection and response assessment in brain metastases, and pediatric-specific modeling aligned with RAPNO. However, AI models remain sensitive to technical and biological variations across institutions, limiting their clinical utility unless appropriate training and validation is performed. Nevertheless, progress is evident in prospective, biopsy-validated infiltration mapping, assessment of resection extent aligned with RANO-Resect, and standardization through AI-RANO. Emerging directions include foundation models, uncertainty estimation, federated learning, AI-enhanced ultra-low-field MRI, and dual-tracer PET. When used as a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for the imaging team, AI can increasingly improve the utility, reproducibility, and efficiency of quantitative, multiparametric imaging in patients with brain tumors.

items.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Topology-Aware Modeling of Multispecific Antibody Function.
items.summary: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. items.abstract: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. Rational design is often bottlenecked by the inability to predict how subtle changes in domain topology influence functional outcomes, a challenge exacerbated by the scarcity of comprehensive experimental data. Here, we introduce Synapse, a biologically inspired synthetic benchmark for topology-aware modeling of msAbs. First, we present a generative method that combines nonlinear per-domain sequence-to-score landscapes with connectivity-dependent synthetic readouts. Second, we propose a graph neural network architecture that explicitly encodes these topological constraints, distinguishing between format configurations that appear identical to the evaluated connectivity-agnostic multilayer perceptron. We demonstrate that this model learns topology-dependent structure-function relationships on synthetic landscapes and evaluate a transfer learning workflow as infrastructure for adaptation to biological datasets. We showcase our framework with a trispecific T cell engager-inspired synthetic topology-dependent optimization task and a constrained ranking of common light chain candidates against a composite objective. This work provides a controlled benchmarking environment for developing and evaluating topology-aware computational tools for msAb modeling. All experiments use synthetic data; no biological validation is performed.

items.abstract: Importance: Leg dystonia affects 50-80% of children with cerebral palsy (CP), but severity assessment remains subjective and time-consuming. Objective tools are urgently needed to quantify leg dystonia severity in clinical care and clinical trials. Objective: To develop and validate a deep neural network (DxToniaNet) for leg dystonia severity estimation using 2D clinical video recordings. Design, Setting, and Participants: We retrospectively analyzed video recordings of 298 children with cerebral palsy undergoing a seated hand open-close task as part of routine clinical care (Center 1: 193 videos, 720p/30fps; Center 2: 105 videos, 4K/60fps). Videos were rated for leg dystonia severity by a group of 7 experts using the Global Dystonia Rating Scale (GDRS) leg subscore (range 0-40) which has a minimum clinically important difference (MCID) of 4 points. Videos displaying leg dystonia (median expert GDRS score ≥1) were used to develop and test a machine learning model (DxToniaNet) for estimating leg dystonia severity. Open-source software (OpenPose) estimated bilateral knee, ankle, and toe coordinates, normalized for height and camera positioning, and 69 variance and amplitude features were calculated based on established expert-cited features of leg dystonia. A neural network, DxToniaNet, was developed, trained and validated using 5-fold cross-validation on Center 1 videos before final testing on independent Center 2 videos. Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s): Mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and accuracy in differentiating between videos with clinically meaningful differences in GDRS scores were calculated relative to experts' median GDRS scores. Results: When estimating experts' leg GDRS scores in testing data, the proposed machine learning (ML) model yielded a MAE of 1.71 ± 1.68 and RMSE of 2.21 ± 0.34 (significantly less than the GDRS MCID of 4), and 90-94% accuracy in differentiating between videos with greater than a 4-point difference in the GDRS. Conclusions and Relevance: We have demonstrated that DxToniaNet can accurately estimate leg dystonia severity compared to experts' assessments with a small (clinically insignificant) error margin. Our methodology supports generalizability since DxToniaNet was developed and tested using independent videos datasets from different centers, recorded under different conditions. In the future, DxToniaNet may help facilitate standardized leg dystonia severity estimation in clinical care and clinical trials.

items.abstract: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is the most effective treatment of a range of severe mental dis-orders and is annually given to more than a million patients worldwide. Dosing of the electrical charge is critical for efficacy and side-effect burden; however, it is currently based on manual assessment of seizure quality and exhibits substantial clinical heterogeneity. Here, we collected 1,000 ECT session electroencephalograms (EEG) from 130 individual ECT patients and made an expert-level classification of the EEGs into actionable seizure quality categories (null-response [0], threshold [T], and adequate [A]). We then trained a range of machine learning algorithms on the raw EEG data to classify the EEGs into these categories and tested for classi-fication accuracy. The highest performing algorithm was able to classify the seizures with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of >0.9 for both the 0 vs. T and the T vs. A categories corresponding to excellent discrimination. In contrast, the accuracy of predicting seizure quality in subsequent treatments was only moderate. The addition of clinical variables to the models, such as demographics, anesthesia and anticonvulsant exposure, did not improve model performance. These results provide proof-of-concept of machine learning classification of seizure adequacy in ECT based on raw EEG data. The findings could pave the way for the de-velopment of more objective and personalized decision-support tools in ECT.

items.abstract: ClinicalTrials.gov provides valuable information for vaccine research, but fragmented data structures and inconsistent vaccine naming complicate systematic cross-trial analysis. The Study-ExperimentAssay Common Data Model (SEA-CDM) provides a standardized structure for biomedical study data, while biomedical ontologies supply semantic relationships among concepts. We extracted 9,147 vaccinerelated study records from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) database, mapped their records into SEA-CDM, and linked vaccine products and reported adverse events (AEs) to the Vaccine Ontology (VO) and Ontology of Adverse Events (OAE), respectively. Building on the existing Ontology-based SEA Network (OSEAN), we organized the integrated data into relational tables and a Neo4j knowledge graph while retaining links to original registrations. We evaluated three applications to assess semantic trial retrieval, context-aware AE ranking and trial similarity, and trial design recommendation. First, VO-based query expansion retrieved 41 candidate RNA vaccine trials compared with 16 using exact VO identifier matching. Second, a context-aware AE ranking model incorporating SEA-CDM features and VO-derived vaccine families improved recall@10 from 0.317 to 0.383 over a frequency-based baseline. TransE and CompGCN embeddings achieved Hits@10 of 0.950 and 0.946, respectively, for retrieving trials sharing the same VO identifier within disease-specific candidate sets. Third, an ontology-based clinical trial design recommendation model was developed using several machine learning methods under leave-one-Material-out evaluation across 23 vaccine classes, although performance varied across classes. These findings demonstrate how structural and semantic integration can support multiple clinical trial analyses using vaccine studies as a case study. This framework provides a foundation for extending ontology-supported data integration and analysis to other clinical research domains.

items.abstract: **Background.** Rule derived (weak) labels can enlarge a training set when reported labels are scarce. Their value depends on label quality, on how the extra records shift the training distribution, and on whether the comparison accounts for reported labels set aside for tuning or calibration. **Methods.** We ran an exploratory label-budget experiment on *Escherichia coli* urine cultures from two de-identified electronic health record datasets: Stanford ARMD and UT Southwestern ARMD-UTSW. The task was to predict reported non-susceptibility to cefepime, cefoxitin and ceftazidime (Stanford) and to cefepime and ceftazidime (UT Southwestern). Reported-label budgets of 10%, 25%, 50% and 100% of development patients were drawn over five patient-disjoint outer splits. Logistic regression and histogram gradient boosting were trained with reported labels only, or with added rule-derived labels using equal weights, a tuning-selected weight, class-proportion adjustment or prior-probability correction. These were compared with an all-budget reported-only baseline that used every budgeted reported label for training. Stanford used the inferred labels released with the dataset and a feature set including resistance history. UT Southwestern used researcher-derived labels from Stanford rule text, which were not validated for that site, and an age-only primary model. Brier-score differences were assessed with paired patient-cluster bootstrap intervals. **Results.** All rule-derived labels were susceptible. Equal-weight augmentation lowered mean predicted risk well below observed prevalence (for example, Stanford cefepime at the 10% budget: 0.35% versus 4.85%) and had a higher Brier score than the all-budget baseline in every drug, model and budget summary. The tuning-selected weight did not consistently improve on the all-budget baseline. Its median Brier difference was positive in 38 of 40 drug, model and budget summaries. Its paired intervals lay above zero in 100 of 296 Stanford analyses and 31 of 198 UT Southwestern analyses, and below zero in 3 and 5. The tuning set often selected a weight of zero (146 of 296 and 153 of 198 analyses). At UT Southwestern, the age-only models showed little discrimination (median AUROC 0.49 to 0.54), so those comparisons mainly reflect calibration. **Conclusions.** Under these designs, rule-derived labels did not consistently improve probability prediction over a reported-only model that used the whole reported-label budget for training. Evaluations of weak supervision should include such a baseline and should report calibration as well as discrimination. **Keywords:** weak supervision; limited-label learning; label budget; probability calibration; class imbalance; antimicrobial resistance

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based computer-aided detection (CAD) of tuberculosis (TB) on chest X-ray (CXR) may standardize screening and triage in settings with few radiologists but its accuracy in clinical cohorts remains uncertain. We searched five databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, OpenAlex, Lens.org) on 15 March 2026 for studies published between January 2020 and March 2026, and we appraised these studies using QUADAS-2. Evaluations from clinical cohorts with complete 2 × 2 data and a microbiological or composite reference standard for all participants were pooled using a bivariate random-effects model, with 95% prediction intervals. We accounted for overlapping participants by performing a post hoc analysis with one evaluation per cohort and used GRADE to assess the certainty of the evidence. No protocol was prepared or registered. We included 21 studies (26 evaluations of AI models). Nine evaluations from three independent cohorts were pooled. Pooled sensitivity was 0.896 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.874 to 0.915, prediction interval 0.798 to 0.950) and pooled specificity was 0.689 (95% CI 0.642 to 0.732; prediction interval 0.499 to 0.831). Both confidence intervals include the World Health Organization (WHO) triage thresholds (sensitivity 90%, specificity 70%). When a screening study with partial verification was added, pooled specificity increased to 0.735. Eighteen of 24 assessed evaluations were at high risk of bias and only 1 of 21 studies was prospective, fully verified, externally validated and met the WHO thresholds. Certainty of evidence was low for sensitivity and very low for specificity. A subsequent PubMed search found additional eligible clinical evaluations that were not screened, so the review is incomplete for those studies. In clinical cohorts, AI-CXR sensitivity is close to the WHO triage target, and specificity is close to, but not clearly above, its target. The evidence is pooled across only three cohorts, and specificity varies by product and setting. Thresholds need to be calibrated locally, and prospective, externally validated evaluations are needed before widespread deployment.

items.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study aimed to investigate the impact of utilizing generative artificial intelligence (AI) as a tool for organizing thoughts and rehearsing prior to consulting clinical instructors on nursing students’ psychological safety and stability, thereby addressing psychological barriers experienced during reporting and consultation in clinical practica. Methods An anonymous, self-administered questionnaire survey consisting of 17 items was conducted among second- to fourth-year nursing students at the School of Medicine, Kochi University. Questionnaire responses were retrieved from a total of 178 patients. We analyzed psychological safety during clinical training, the status of generative AI utilization, and student expectations and perceived challenges regarding its use. Comparative analyses were performed across academic years and between two groups stratified by expectation level toward AI utilization (high- vs. low-expectation groups). Results Third-year students, who were commencing domain-specific clinical practica, exhibited the highest anxiety regarding asking questions to clinical instructors. Concurrently, they demonstrated the greatest reduction in perceived burden when formulating nursing care plans using AI, alongside the highest intention for future active AI utilization. Compared with the low-expectation group, the high-expectation group exhibited significantly more positive perceptions regarding psychological safety scores (2.5 vs. 2.9, P < 0.001) and psychological impact scores (2.1 vs. 3.3, P < 0.001). Conclusion These findings suggest that generative AI functions as an effective psychological buffer to lower interpersonal barriers, thereby enhancing nursing students’ psychological safety during clinical training.

items.abstract: Abstract Responsibility for artificial intelligence (AI) assisted medical decisions encompasses both preventing harm and providing a way to respond when harm occurs. These functions are often combined in empirical measures of accountability, making it difficult to identify which safeguards respondents prioritise. This cross-sectional analysis used 385 adult responses to a common questionnaire on AI, health law and patient rights in Bangladesh. Three preventive statements addressed defined responsibility, independent clinical judgement and organisational and developer safety controls. A separate statement addressed access to complaints and remedies; a fifth elicited anticipated trust under clear accountability. Endorsement was compared within respondents using exact McNemar tests with Holm adjustment. Exploratory regression distinguished prevention and redress as correlates of anticipated trust. Redress was endorsed by 311 respondents (80.8%), exceeding endorsement of each preventive statement by 16.6–20.5 percentage points (all adjusted p < 0.001). The adjusted linear association with anticipated trust was positive for the prevention summary (b = 0.205, 95% CI 0.049 to 0.361; adjusted p = 0.020), but attenuated in inference when trust was dichotomised. The redress coefficient was close to zero in the adjusted linear model (b = 0.001, 95% CI −0.112 to 0.114). These findings distinguish broad endorsement of a patient-facing remedy from covariance with a hypothetical trust judgement. They support evaluating complaint access as a governance outcome in its own right. The survey neither verifies actual use of medical AI nor estimates effects of introducing safeguards.

items.abstract: Abstract Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects 20--50% of ICU admissions, and the optimal timing for renal replacement therapy (RRT) initiation remains contested. Methods: We developed and externally validated a leakage-safe, causal-weighted machine learning pipeline predicting 48-hour RRT initiation in patients with KDIGO stage 3 AKI, using harmonized MIMIC-IV and eICU data. A regularized stacking ensemble with inverse-probability-weighted meta-learning combined five base learners (LightGBM, XGBoost, Random Forest, CatBoost, ExtraTrees) via a logistic-regression meta-learner. Results: The model achieved AUC 0.894 internally and 0.807 on an independent, 200+ hospital external cohort, significantly outperforming four of five baseline models (DeLong \((p<0.001)\)) while remaining statistically indistinguishable from a single LightGBM model. Stacking-consistent SHAP identified creatinine and urine output trajectories as dominant risk drivers, 40% of high-risk patients had a feasible short-term recourse below threshold, and fairness assessment showed no clinically meaningful subgroup gaps. Conclusions: A prototype clinical decision support system operationalizes the model for bedside use, motivating prospective evaluation before deployment.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Depressive symptoms are common among people living with HIV (PLHIV) and are associated with poorer antiretroviral therapy (ART) adherence and viral suppression. In rural settings, routine symptom screening may be constrained by counsellor workload and limited specialist mental health capacity. This study developed and internally evaluated ten supervised machine-learning (ML) models for identifying PHQ-9-defined probable depression among PLHIV attending ART clinics in Kadjebi District, Ghana. Methods A facility-based cross-sectional dataset of 264 adults receiving ART was analysed. Probable depression was defined as a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score of 10 or above. Fifty-two predictors were engineered from sociodemographic, HIV-clinical, tuberculosis-service, physical-health, psychosocial, stigma and health-system variables; the nine PHQ-9 items were excluded from predictors. Data were partitioned 80:20 with stratification. Imputation and, where required, standardisation were fitted using the training partition, and SMOTE was applied only to the training data. Ten algorithms were tuned using five-fold cross-validation within the training partition. Performance on the untouched held-out test set was treated as the primary split-sample internal validation, with 5-fold x 4-repeat cross-validation of the training partition used as a secondary stability analysis. Performance metrics included AUC, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1 score, Cohen's kappa, Brier score and calibration slope. Interpretability used permutation importance and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP); decision-curve analysis was exploratory. Results PHQ-9-defined probable depression was present in 100 of 264 participants (37.9%). Random Forest was selected by the training-set cross-validation results. On the held-out test set, it achieved an AUC of 0.870, accuracy of 77.4%, sensitivity of 80.0%, specificity of 75.8%, F1 score of 0.727, Cohen's kappa of 0.536 and Brier score of 0.137. Its secondary repeated-cross-validation AUC was 0.893 (SD 0.041). Differences in cross-validated AUC among the leading algorithms were small relative to fold-to-fold variability, and no formal pairwise superiority testing was performed. Permutation importance and SHAP consistently highlighted comfort disclosing psychological difficulty, belief system, counselling and tailored mental-health service availability, perceived healthcare access and quality, sex, and perceived HIV impact. Exploratory decision-curve analysis suggested potential net benefit of model-guided PHQ-9 administration; at a threshold of 0.40, 48.9% of attendees would receive the PHQ-9 while 94% of PHQ-9-positive cases would be identified. This calculation concerns PHQ-9 administrations only and does not quantify total workflow burden. At the PHQ-9 > = 5 sensitivity threshold, Random Forest had a secondary cross-validated AUC of 0.911. Conclusion Random Forest showed promising discrimination for PHQ-9-defined probable depression in this small, single-district development study, but the findings remain proof-of-concept. Relational and service-related variables contributed strongly to prediction. Threshold analyses suggest that risk stratification could reduce the number of PHQ-9 administrations, but total counselling burden and safety were not established. External validation, development of a more parsimonious routine-workflow model, and prospective evaluation are required before clinical use; a prediction model should not replace assessment of suicide or self-harm risk.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Efficient early identification of individuals at risk of developing psychotic disorders or bipolar disorders is crucial and challenging to improving mental health outcomes in adolescents. Objective neurophysiological and neurobehavioral measures may provide information complementary to conventional symptom-based assessment. Electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-tracking offer non-invasive and relatively accessible measures of neural and behavioral function and may support longitudinal risk detection for psychotic disorders or bipolar disorders. This study aims to prospectively evaluate and develop early recognition models for adolescents at high risk for psychotic or bipolar disorders using EEG and eye-tracking features. Methods This is a prospective, observational, single-centre longitudinal cohort study conducted at Peking University Sixth Hospital. A total of 300 adolescents aged 12–19 years at elevated risk for psychotic or bipolar disorder (BD) will be recruited. Baseline assessments will include diagnostic interviews, clinician-rated and self-report symptom measures, psychosocial functioning assessments, cognitive tasks, and simultaneous EEG and eye-tracking recording. Participants will undergo clinical reassessments at 6, 12, 18, and 24 months. The primary objective is to identify the specific EEG and eye-tracking features associated with adverse clinical progression over 2 years in adolescents at elevated risk for psychotic disorders or bipolar disorder, and to develop and validate the risk-stratification prediction models based on synchronized EEG and eye-tracking data. Secondary objectives include estimating the rate and temporal pattern of diagnostic transition to psychotic disorder or BD, characterizing longitudinal trajectories of psychiatric symptoms and psychosocial functioning, and evaluating the incremental prognostic value of digital phenotype markers beyond conventional clinical assessment. Statistical analyses will include Cox proportional hazards models, linear mixed-effects models, and machine learning approaches with feature selection and internal validation. Discussion This study applies a longitudinal multimodal framework to investigate the developmental trajectories of adolescents at elevated risk for psychotic disorders or BD. By deriving EEG-eye-tracking fusion digital biomarkers, this study aims to clarify whether integrating objective neurophysiological and behavioral measures can improve individual-level prediction of adverse clinical progression beyond traditional clinical assessment. Findings from this cohort may provide preliminary evidence for precision risk monitoring and inform future preventive strategies for severe mental disorders in youth. items.abstract: Abstract Background; Obstetric hemorrhage and hypertensive disorders drive Ethiopia’s high maternal mortality ratio (267/100000 live births), requiring continuous availability of lifesaving maternal commodities (LMCs). Conventional statistics offer retrospective insights rather than facility level risk forecasting. This study developed and validated machine learning classifiers to predict LMC stock outs in Ethiopian primary healthcare facilities using EDHS 2024/2025 data. Methods; A secondary analysis evaluated 1245 primary facilities. The binary outcome measured physical absence, expiration or recent stock outs of any 5 WHO tracer commodities. Nineteen features spanning logistics, human resources and infrastructure were analyzed. Five algorithms Logistic Regression, SVC, MLP-ANN, Random Forest and XGBoost were implemented, handling class imbalance via SMOTE and evaluating performance via ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Decision Curve Analysis (DCA), probability calibration and SHAP interpretability. Results; Overall, 45.8% of facilities experienced stock outs. XGBoost outperformed other models on the test set, achieving a ROC-AUC of 0.894, Accuracy of 88.8%, Sensitivity of 89.5% and Specificity of 88.1%. It exhibited high reliability (Brier Score of 0.084) and superior net clinical benefit via DCA across thresholds from 10% to 85%. SHAP analysis identified non-functional cold chain equipment, lack of IPLS reporting, absence of APTS auditing, irregular bin card reconciliation and lack of professional pharmacy personnel as the top risk drivers. Conclusion; Supervised machine learning algorithms notably XGBoost accurately forecast maternal commodity stock outs. Integrating this architecture into the national eLMIS enables proactive risk flagging, helping the Ministry of Health and EPSS prioritize cold chain upgrades, digital logistics and staffing in vulnerable facilities.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Endometrial cancer (EC) is strongly associated with metabolic disorders, while glycolytic reprogramming contributes to tumor progression and adverse outcomes. This study aimed to identify glycolysis-related prognostic genes and develop a machine learning-based signature for EC risk stratification. Methods Transcriptomic and clinical data were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas. Glycolysis-related genes were collected from KEGG, MSigDB, and Reactome. Differential expression and univariate Cox analyses were used to identify prognostic candidates. Multiple machine learning algorithms and combinations were evaluated to construct a prognostic model. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, somatic mutation, tumor mutational burden, and drug sensitivity analyses were performed. Single-cell RNA sequencing datasets GSE179640 and GSE173682 were analyzed to characterize CENPA expression across cell types and its clinical relevance. Results Among 5,990 differentially expressed genes, 99 overlapped with 290 glycolysis-related genes, and 16 were associated with overall survival. Among 117 model combinations, random survival forest plus generalized boosted model generated a seven-gene signature comprising CLDN9, CENPA, GPI, TFF3, FBP1, SPAG4, and AURKA. The 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs were 0.88, 0.81, and 0.84 in the training cohort and 0.73, 0.77, and 0.76 in the internal validation cohort, respectively. High-risk patients had poorer survival and distinct pathway, immune, and genomic features. Single-cell analysis showed heterogeneous CENPA expression, while elevated CENPA was associated with advanced stage and poorer survival. Conclusions The glycolysis-related signature stratified EC patients by survival risk and was associated with distinct biological features. CENPA emerged as a candidate prognostic biomarker requiring independent external validation and experimental investigation.

items.abstract: Abstract Traffic calming is recognized as a set of physical interventions aimed at reducing vehicle speeds and enhancing the safety of vulnerable road users. However, speed bumps and speed humps can exert considerable adverse effects on patients, occupants, and drivers. This study aimed to conduct multi-scale modeling of the effects of optimizing the number and location of speed bumps and speed humps on these three groups. To this end, a convolutional neural network was employed to determine the optimal number of obstacles across 48 urban roadways. Subsequently, the effects of reducing obstacles on eight patient groups (cardiovascular, spinal, intubated, CPR, post-surgical, pregnant women, osteoporosis, and stroke) and on occupant and driver groups were quantified using biomechanical and clinical models. The results indicated that scenario S5, with 39 speed bumps and 45 speed humps, exhibits the best performance, achieving a 51.3% reduction in the number of speed bumps and a 55.9% reduction in the number of speed humps compared with the existing condition. This reduction led to a 51.7% decrease in the cumulative driver anger index, a 51.3% reduction in zero occupant comfort, a 42.6% reduction in cardiovascular risk, a 66.7% reduction in endotracheal tube displacement, and a 45.5% improvement in CPR quality. Dynamic analysis using the reference vehicle demonstrated that although the road acceleration at speed bumps is 16.8 times that at speed humps, due to suspension damping, the actual acceleration on the vehicle seat is only 22.8 times greater, and the actual VDV is approximately 3.3 times greater. The findings indicate that reducing the number of speed bumps takes higher priority than reducing speed humps.

items.abstract: Abstract Background: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) followed by total mesorectal excision is standard for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). While tumor regression grade is routinely reported, lymph node regression grade (LRG) is underutilized. We aimed to develop a machine learning model for preoperative LRG prediction. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 111 LARC patients who underwent nCRT plus surgery between January 2016 and December 2020. LRGmax (grades 0–5) was assessed using Mandard criteria. Elastic Net regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for feature selection, followed by a Softmax multinomial classifier. Patients were randomly split into training (70%) and validation (30%) sets. Performance was evaluated using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and recall. Bootstrap resampling and decision curve analysis assessed calibration and clinical net benefit. Results: The LRGmax distribution was: grade 0 (28.8%), 1 (39.6%), 2 (12.6%), 3 (10.8%), 4 (5.4%), and 5 (2.7%). In the training set, AUC was 0.99. In the validation set, AUC was 0.86 and specificity 0.87. Calibration curves showed high consistency; DCA revealed positive net benefit. Higher LRGmax correlated with increased nodal metastasis count, lymph node ratio, and worse survival (all P < 0.001). LRGmax correlated positively with radiotherapy efficacy ( r = 0.28, P = 0.003) and negatively with 3-year survival ( r = –0.47, P < 0.001). Conclusions: The Elastic Net–Softmax model showed discriminative utility for predicting LRGmax after nCRT in LARC. Despite decreased validation metrics due to limited sample size and class imbalance, the model retained predictive value as a proof-of-concept tool. Multi-center prospective studies are warranted.

items.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) populations are characterized by a high prevalence of non-infectious virions, with particle-to-plaque forming unit (PFU) ratios typically ranging from 10 to 1,000. While "multiplicity reactivation" -the process by which incomplete viral genomes (IVGs) establish productive infection through co-infection- has long been hypothesized, its quantitative nature has remained elusive. In this study, we utilized a digital influenza assay to achieve absolute quantification of IAV particles, allowing us to define the particle-based multiplicity of infection (pMOI) for precise evaluation. We combined this approach with a single-cell infection assay using microcompartmentalized containers and machine learning-based automated cell classification to accurately assess infection outcomes across a wide range of pMOIs. Our analysis of the A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1) revealed a count-to-plaque forming unit (PFU) ratio of approximately 400, meaning only a tiny fraction of particles possesses infectivity. Remarkably, the infection rate in single-cell infection experiments followed a sigmoidal curve and reached saturation at a pMOI of only 5 to 10. This demonstrates that under high-pMOI conditions, productive infection is predominantly driven by genome complementation among incomplete particles rather than solely by fully infectious virions. On the other hand, mathematical model analysis based on these findings suggested that the functionality of each of the eight genomic segments within a virus particle follows a stochastic process, resulting in a probability distribution for the number of functional segments per particle. This mechanism proved exceptionally robust across multiple strains despite a 20-fold variation in CTPR values. Ultimately, these findings indicate that incomplete particles are not merely biological noise but active contributors to the infection process, significantly enhancing the infectivity and evolutionary flexibility of IAV. This study will provide a more refined understanding of influenza transmission dynamics and risk assessment, particularly in environments where multiple virus particles are present within a single respiratory droplet.
